title: Interviewer introduces the Cakewalkin' Babies portion of the tape
summary: The interviewer says the preceding music was Frank Chace and Marty Grosz in a Chicago style and that the University of Chicago Cakewalkin' Babies, imitating early New Orleans records, follow.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: guitar solo guitar solo guitar solo guitar solo guitar solo Up to this point, we've been listening to Frank Chase and Marty Gross playing in what might be called a Chicago style, influenced by what they heard on records of the Harlem musicians, the swing musicians, the New Orleans musicians, the Revival Dixieland and so forth. And from this point on, we will hear the University of Chicago band called the Cakewalkin' Babies, who are playing largely in a style imitative or derivative of the early New Orleans records, most of which were made by New Orleans men around Chicago in the early 20s. the personnel and tunes are given on a listing which accompanies this tape. guitar solo guitar solo guitar solo Thank you.
